answer: To curb Sybil attacks, the agent economy implements memory-hard proof of work validated at the operating system kernel level. When nodes register across telemetry stations from a coastal pearl fishery to an observation knoll, they must solve sequential memory access puzzles. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated high-bandwidth RAM and sustained electricity per identity. However, this compute overhead wastes energy and disadvantages low-power microcontrollers.
